summary.name: Hubzilla
summary.one_liner: Hubzilla is an open source, privacy-focused all-in-one fediverse server that combines social networking, groups and forums, cloud file storage, and blogging.
use_cases: Share private or restricted files with friends
Run moderated federated discussion groups or forums
Blog, publish pages, or maintain a wiki
Move or back up your online identity to another server
Log into other websites using your account
summary.what_it_does: Hubzilla lets users connect with people across the Fediverse (such as Mastodon, Misskey, and PeerTube) via ActivityPub and Diaspora. It provides privacy and access control over posts, web pages, articles, wikis, images, and files, with public, private, or restricted permissions. Users can create public or private discussion groups and forums, and share cloud storage files. Blog, page, and wiki features support HTML, BBCode, and Markdown. It also offers nomadic identity, where a channel can be cloned to another server as a synced backup or downloaded, and federated single sign-on for logging into other sites.
notable: Nomadic identity: transfer, clone, or back up your identity to another server
Federated single sign-on to log into other websites without a local account
Conversation containers with extra moderation tools
Supports ActivityPub, Diaspora, and other fediverse protocols
caveats: Page does not name specific platforms beyond being web-based; server installation requirements are not stated on the page
